content: The Battle Creek Sanitarium, located in Battle Creek, Michigan, United States, was originally established on September 5, 1866, under the name Western Health Reform Institute. Its foundation was based on the health principles promoted by the Seventh-day Adventist Church. In 1876, Dr. John Harvey Kellogg assumed the role of superintendent, while his brother, W.K. Kellogg, worked as the institution's bookkeeper. In 1878, a new building was constructed on the site, but it was destroyed by fire in 1902. The following year, the facility was rebuilt and expanded. In 1942, the United States Army purchased the complex and repurposed it as the Percy Jones Army Hospital, which was used to treat soldiers injured during World War II. Notable U.S. senators, including Philip Hart, Bob Dole, and Daniel Inouye, received treatment at this hospital. The Battle Creek Sanitarium was officially listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1976. Over its history, it hosted more than 400,000 guests, including 1,800 staff members, and became a popular destination for both prominent and middle-class Americans. Among its notable visitors were celebrated figures such as Mary Todd Lincoln and Sojourner Truth, whose presence helped inspire public enthusiasm for health and wellness. The sanitarium was affectionately nicknamed The San by its patrons and became a favored retreat for the wealthy, offering health-focused vacations and dieting programs. Dr. John Harvey Kellogg implemented a variety of treatments for his patients at the sanitarium, emphasizing dietary reform and frequent enemas. He advocated for a low-fat, low-protein diet that prioritized whole grains, fiber-rich foods, and, most importantly, nuts. Additionally, he stressed the importance of daily fresh air, regular exercise, and personal hygiene. Many of his health theories were later compiled and published in his book, The Road to Wellness. The sanitarium and Dr. Kellogg were later satirized in the 1993 novel The Road to Wellville and its 1994 film adaptation of the same name.
